label: Whatever has its being caused by another has its esse received in some principle
paraphrase: Open bridge, analyst formulation, unattributed. For all c and x: if c is distinct from x and c causes x's being (CausesIn c x esse), then x's esse is received in some principle (EsseReceivedIn x z for some z: a principle standing to it as receiving potency to received act, DEF-ESSE-RECEIVED-IN). After ST I q.7 a.2 (the esse of a subsistent created form is received and contracted) and De ente c.4 (what has esse from another receives it), generalized to everything caused as to being; the generalization is the analyst's. It joins, as one explicit premise, the two notions DISAMB-ESSE-RECEPTION keeps apart: origin from another and reception in a principle. Its own Lean does not use Creature. Since 2026-11-12 it is also derived (specs/creature-senses.toml, causedEsseIsReceivedThroughCreature1) through the typed CREATURE senses (DISAMB c49de1e9-c34f-424f-b144-b80c885974ca): whatever is CREATURE_2 (caused in being by another) is CREATURE_1 (caused in being by a universal cause of being; the sense bridge, itself derived from the proved Fourth-Way consequence STMT-MAXIMAL-CAUSE-WITHOUT-DISTINCT-ESSE-CAUSE and the weak premise that whatever has its being caused is in act as to being), and the esse of every CREATURE_1 is received in some principle (the q.7 a.2 reading, at the sense q.7 a.2 speaks of). The generalization from things made by God to everything caused as to being then rests on the Fourth Way's universal causation of being, not on this bridge. It does not say the principle is the thing's own essence (that is STMT-ESSE-RECEIVED-IN-OWN-ESSENCE), nor what the principle really is. SCOPE CONDITION (definition 80dea550): elements of Being are individuated by their act of being, so the divine processions are no instances of CausesIn c x esse with c distinct from x; read with them as instances, the bridge would give the Son received, and with STMT-RECEIVED-ESSE-IS-LIMITED limited, esse, contrary to the case's Nicene commitment. Unread lead, no evidential weight: the tradition denying a real distinction of esse and essence in creatures (Scotus, Ockham, later metaphysics; lead text Suarez, Disputationes metaphysicae 31) would target this bridge if the receiving principle must be really distinct; it would reject this route to finitude, not the finitude of caused things.
